Let
\[
h(x)=x^2-\frac45x+\frac1{10},
\qquad
R(x)=x^2+\frac{13}{5}x+\frac{108}{25}.
\]
On \([0,1]\), \(R(x)>0\), so
\[
q(x)=(1-x)h(x)^2R(x)\ge 0.
\]
A direct check of the top coefficients shows
\[
p(x):=x^7+q(x)
\]
is actually a polynomial of degree at most \(4\). Hence for every admissible \(X\),
\[
X^7\le p(X),
\]
so
\[
\mathbb E[X^7]\le \mathbb E[p(X)].
\]
Since \(p\) has degree at most \(4\), its expectation is fixed by the given moments.

Now take the roots of \(h\):
\[
\alpha=\frac{4-\sqrt6}{10},\qquad \beta=\frac{4+\sqrt6}{10}.
\]
Consider the measure with atoms
\[
\alpha,\ \beta,\ 1
\]
and weights
\[
\frac49-\frac{\sqrt6}{36},\qquad
\frac49+\frac{\sqrt6}{36},\qquad
\frac19.
\]
These weights are positive and sum to \(1\). The two non-endpoint roots satisfy
\[
z^2=\frac45z-\frac1{10},
\]
so their weighted power sums obey the recurrence
\[
\mu_{k+2}=\frac45\mu_{k+1}-\frac1{10}\mu_k.
\]
Starting from \(\mu_0=8/9,\ \mu_1=7/18\), this gives
\[
\mu_2=\frac29,\quad \mu_3=\frac5{36},\quad \mu_4=\frac4{45}.
\]
Adding the endpoint contribution \(1/9\) gives
\[
1,\ \frac12,\ \frac13,\ \frac14,\ \frac15,
\]
so this measure is admissible.

For the seventh moment, the same recurrence gives
\[
\mu_5=\frac{103}{1800},\qquad
\mu_6=\frac{83}{2250},\qquad
\mu_7=\frac{2141}{90000}.
\]
Including the atom at \(1\),
\[
\mathbb E[X^7]=\frac{2141}{90000}+\frac19
=\frac{2141}{90000}+\frac{10000}{90000}
=\frac{12141}{90000}
=\frac{1349}{10000}.
\]

Because the polynomial majorant gives this same upper bound and the atomic distribution attains it, the maximum is

\[
\boxed{\frac{1349}{10000}}.
\]
